name: Call a Hosted Microsoft Foundry Agent (and a Bedrock Agent) From a Workflow, Serving Its Function Tool With a Worker
query: Our finance team built an agent in Microsoft Foundry (endpoint `https://finance-ai.services.ai.azure.com`, assistant id `asst_abc123`) with a function tool `get_revenue(region, quarter)` that Foundry can't execute itself — we have the code for it. I want a Conductor workflow that calls the Foundry agent with a prompt and somehow runs `get_revenue` for it, authenticating with an Azure service principal. We also have a Bedrock agent (agent id `AGENT123`, alias `ALIAS456`, us-east-1) — same question. And someone asked about a Vertex agent.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agents.md §9 (hosted platform agents: `prompt` required; `credentials{}` with values via `${workflow.secrets.CRED.key}` — the secret must be a JSON object for sub-keys; `agentUrl` or `rawConfig`; auth chosen by which credential keys are present; `autoRunTools` on by default → each function-tool call runs as a SIMPLE task named after the tool with inputs flattened + `_toolCallId`, `_toolName`, `_agentExecutionId`, tasks `optional`; `maxToolTurns` default 10; `toolTaskNames`; `autoRunTools: false` → `waiting: true` + `pendingTools`, manual resume with `toolResults` keyed by `tool_call_id`; Bedrock has no status or cancel API; Foundry runs expire 10 minutes after creation; `azure-foundry` is a deprecated alias; no `vertex` runtime → `agentType: "a2a"`), references/workflow-definition.md (`### AGENT` — `agentType` modes; `autoRunTools` / `maxToolTurns` / `toolTaskNames` row), references/optimization.md F1, F7, D1, and the `/conductor-scaffold-worker` command for the `get_revenue` worker.

Step 2: Foundry task: `{"name":"ask_finance","taskReferenceName":"ask_finance","type":"AGENT","inputParameters":{"agentType":"microsoft-foundry","prompt":"${workflow.input.question}","credentials":{"client_id":"${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CRED.client_id}","client_secret":"${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CRED.client_secret}","tenant_id":"${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CRED.tenant_id}"},"rawConfig":{"endpoint":"https://finance-ai.services.ai.azure.com","assistantId":"asst_abc123"},"maxToolTurns":10,"pollIntervalSeconds":5,"maxDurationSeconds":540}}` — `agentUrl` (`https://<res>.../assistants/asst_x`) is the one-field alternative to `rawConfig`; `azure-foundry` still works as a deprecated alias.

Step 3: Secret shape: `AZURE_CRED` must be a JSON object `{"client_id":"...","client_secret":"...","tenant_id":"..."}` so `${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CRED.client_id}` resolves (OSS: `CONDUCTOR_SECRET_AZURE_CRED` env on the server; Orkes: secret manager). Never pass credentials via `${workflow.input.*}` (D1). Auth is selected by the keys present: `client_id`+`client_secret`+`tenant_id` → service principal; `apiKey` → key auth; `managedIdentityClientId`; none → default chain.

Step 4: The tool loop: with `autoRunTools` (default true) the `AGENT` task stays `IN_PROGRESS`, schedules a SIMPLE task named `get_revenue` whose input is the tool's arguments flattened (`region`, `quarter`) plus `_toolCallId`, `_toolName`, `_agentExecutionId` (the task is `optional`), then resumes the Foundry run with the result. So a worker registered for task type `get_revenue` (scaffold with `/conductor-scaffold-worker` or `@worker_task(task_definition_name="get_revenue")`) serves the agent's tool with no extra wiring; `maxToolTurns` (10) bounds the rounds; `toolTaskNames: {"get_revenue": "finance_get_revenue"}` remaps if the worker has another name. Alternative `autoRunTools: false`: the task completes with `waiting: true` + `pendingTools` and you resume with `executionId` + `toolResults` keyed by `tool_call_id`.

Step 5: Bedrock variant: `{"agentType":"bedrock","prompt":"${workflow.input.question}","agentUrl":"bedrock://AGENT123/ALIAS456?region=us-east-1","credentials":{"roleArn":"${workflow.secrets.AWS_CRED.roleArn}"},"maxToolTurns":10,"maxDurationSeconds":540}` (or `rawConfig: {agentId, agentAliasId, region}`; or `accessKeyId` + `secretAccessKey` keys). Same `autoRunTools` behaviour. Bedrock has no status or cancel API — the call is terminal on the first response, so `CANCEL_AGENT` cannot stop it mid-flight.

Step 6: Foundry runs expire 10 minutes after creation, total — keep the `get_revenue` worker fast, keep `maxToolTurns` small and set `maxDurationSeconds` under 600 s; F1 also wants a workflow `timeoutSeconds`.

Step 7: Vertex: there is no `vertex` `agentType` — expose the Vertex agent over A2A and call it with `agentType: "a2a"` + `agentUrl` (examples/agent-a2a-remote.md). Mention `openai-assistants` as the third hosted type (`rawConfig.assistantId`, `baseUrl`). Never a framework name as `agentType` (F7).

Step 8: Outputs: `${ask_finance.output.text}`, plus `executedTools`, `pendingTools`, `toolDispatchId`. Write the JSON to a file, `conductor workflow create <file>`; start the `get_revenue` worker before `conductor workflow start` (Rule 1); never `conductor deploy` (nothing to deploy — the agent lives on the platform).
success_criteria: The Foundry task is `type: "AGENT"` with `agentType: "microsoft-foundry"` (noting `azure-foundry` as a deprecated alias) and a `prompt`

`credentials` carries `client_id` / `client_secret` / `tenant_id` from the secrets system — either one JSON-object secret with sub-keys (`${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CRED.client_id}`) or three flat secrets (`${workflow.secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID}`, …) — and never via `${workflow.input.*}`
The target is given via `rawConfig: {endpoint, assistantId}` or an `agentUrl`

Explains `autoRunTools` (default on): the agent's `get_revenue` call runs as a SIMPLE task named after the tool inside the parent workflow, served by a worker, and the result is fed back to the Foundry run (naming the `_toolCallId` / `_toolName` / `_agentExecutionId` inputs is a plus)
Bounds the hosted tool loop with `maxToolTurns` (default 10); mentioning `toolTaskNames` remapping or the `autoRunTools: false` → `pendingTools` / `toolResults` manual path is a plus

Bedrock variant uses `agentType: "bedrock"` with `agentUrl: "bedrock://AGENT123/ALIAS456?region=us-east-1"` (or `rawConfig` `agentId` / `agentAliasId` / `region`) and `roleArn` or access-key credentials via secrets
States that Bedrock has no status / cancel API and that Foundry runs expire 10 minutes after creation
States there is no `vertex` `agentType` and points to `agentType: "a2a"` for Vertex agents (mentioning `openai-assistants` as the third hosted type is a plus)

Never uses a framework name or an invented `"azure"` / `"foundry"` / `"vertex"` as `agentType`; any `model` field that appears is `provider/model`; `maxDurationSeconds` and/or a workflow timeout are set (F1)
Workflow JSON is written to a file before `conductor workflow create`, a worker for `get_revenue` is scaffolded or stated as running before the start, and `conductor deploy` is never used
